name: array-stats
title: Array statistics
summary: A week of step counts from a float array: bars scaled by arrayMax, the best day highlighted by a step mask, an average line, and total, average, best and standard deviation computed with arraySum, arrayLength, arrayMax and arraySumSqr.
prompt: Show a week of step counts as a bar chart with the best day highlighted and an average line, and summary stats on top: total, average, best day and standard deviation.
teaches: Aggregate an array inside expressions: arraySum(@a), arrayLength(@a), arrayMax(@a), arrayMin(@a), arrayGet(@a, i)
Compute an average once as a named variable (avg = arraySum / arrayLength) and a standard deviation as sqrt(arraySumSqr(@a) / arrayLength(@a) − square(@avg))
Highlight the maximum without a branch: alpha 0.45 + 0.55 * step(arrayGet(@a, i), arrayMax(@a) − 1)
Print large numbers with thousands separators (flags 21: 16 GROUPING_BY3 + 5) and round in the expression with round()
pitfalls: There is no arrayAvg in JSON (the runtime has one): divide arraySum by arrayLength
textFromFloat with decimal 0 cuts the fraction (8385.7 prints 8385) unless the rounding flag 512 is set; round() in the expression does the same and keeps the flags simple
floatArrays are exported by default: a host can replace the week's values and every statistic follows

Bars placed at 29 + i * 45.714 only span the header width: derive the slot from componentWidth() ((@r - 20) / 7) so they spread over any width, and scale the chart down as a whole where the four figures would no longer fit

The values are labelled on the canvas to keep the lesson on expressions in one place (rc-inspect flags it: text_in_canvas). In a real screen put labels and values in text components around the drawing.

snippets.note: bars scaled by arrayGet / arrayMax; the best day's mask from step()

check.describe: Seven bars, Saturday tallest and brighter; a yellow average line at about 70 % of the tallest; the stats read 58,700 total, 8,386 average, 12,100 best day and 2,139 standard deviation. Resized, below the 360 design width the chart is scaled down as a whole (@s = min(1, w / 360)) and centred vertically, so the four figures still fit on one line at 234 wide; wider, the figures spread over quarters and the bars over sevenths of the live width (@r = componentWidth() / @s - 20), at 540 wide too.
